ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer: confirm from the path record whether the 12:29–12:39 off-route segment (F3) was actually driven on Sims Avenue, the road the rider agreed to (F8, F9). If it was, no refund (RD-5); if not, refund 3.27 km × $1.4098/km = $4.61 (RD-2), and decide separately on the $0.11 metered waiting unit (F5, RD-3(c)).
ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so distance actually driven enters the fare; the record shows one off-route segment, F3, 12:29–12:39, driving 6.34 km where the optimal route covers 3.07 km, adding 3.27 km and straying up to 755 m from the optimal route [F3], against an overall 19.4 km vs 15.5 km optimal and 32.2 min vs 21.8 min [F1][F2]. Under RD-1 that segment is subject to RD-3 / RD-4 / RD-5 review, and if unexempted it is refundable under RD-2.

The RD-4 screen is settled against the driver: the trace marks the incident limb ✗ — no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window [F14] — and the only congestion record, PIE speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 12:04–12:29 [F12], is at most corroboration under RD-4(b), which the MVP default does not let exempt a segment on its own; fair weather [F15] supplies no other reasonable cause. Both advocates concede this. So RD-4 excuses nothing here.

The rider's consent is real and pre-segment: the driver asked at 12:26 whether he could "go round via Sims Avenue" because PIE traffic was building up [F8], and the rider herself replied at 12:27 "Sure, go ahead." [F9], before the segment's 12:29 start [F3]; the chat record is complete with every message timestamped [F10]. That is a rider message sent before the segment, so RD-5 is engaged. But its scope is a SPECIFIC named road: F9's words answer F8's named-road ask, so the permission runs to driving on Sims Avenue only, not a general route licence — the trace's kind (2).

What the record cannot settle is the correspondence RD-5 and G13 require: the fact table carries no road name for the path actually driven, no chat message or stop places the car on Sims Avenue during 12:29–12:39, and F3 gives only time and distance [F3][F8][F9][F10]; the driver's own post-trip statement naming Sims Avenue [F11] is a statement, not consent, and cannot tie the segment to the road (G11). Nor does any fact place the segment somewhere else, so it cannot be converted into an unagreed detour or a driver errand. Both advocates state the same ground for F3 — named road, untied — and that stipulation binds. The finding is therefore undetermined, which under G13 and RD-5 changes the amount and sends the case to a person.

Because the segment is undetermined, the amount cannot be executed: if the segment was driven on Sims Avenue it is exempt under RD-5 and nothing is refundable; if it was not, RD-2 gives 3.27 km × the trace's per-km rate ($27.35 ÷ 19.40 km = $1.4098/km) = $4.61 [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]. The billed excess of $5.54 for 3.93 km [F4] does not cap or expand that figure, and the corridor gap is not refunded. The $0.11 metered waiting unit [F5] is waiting, not distance, and on RydeTAXI is charged at the meter regardless of the segment's status; whether it follows the segment is for the human reviewer together with the segment finding (RD-3(c)). RD-6 is not met: the driver's two upheld disputes in 90 days include zero route disputes [F17], so no account flag is warranted.

segment_findings.reason: The rider agreed under RD-5 before the segment (F9 at 12:27 answers the driver's 12:26 ask in F8), but only to the named road Sims Avenue, and no fact ties the driven 12:29–12:39 segment to that road: F3 gives time and distance only, F10 shows no further message, and the driver's post-trip statement F11 cannot establish the tie (G11). No fact places the segment elsewhere either, so it is not an unagreed detour on this record — RD-5 + G13 make the finding undetermined, which changes the amount.

rejected_claims.reason: The RD-2 per-km arithmetic is right (F4, F7), but RD-2 only bites on an unexempted segment; F3's status under RD-5 is undetermined, so no refund can be executed on this record.

The $0.11 metered waiting unit (F5) is waiting time, not detour distance; on RydeTAXI it is charged at the meter regardless of the segment's status (RD-3(c)), so it does not follow the segment automatically.
The rider's message at 12:27 before the 12:29 segment (F9, F3) is accepted as pre-segment consent, but RD-5 limits it to the named road Sims Avenue, which no record ties to the segment.
The driver's own reading that no road name ties the segment (F3, F10) is accepted, but that leaves the RD-5 scope undetermined, which changes the amount — it does not yield no_action.
A lone PIE speed band 2 reading for 12:04–12:29 (F12) cannot corroborate driving on the 12:29–12:39 segment (F3), and under RD-4(b) a band alone does not exempt a segment.
The maximum-exposure framing from F4/F7 is accepted, but RD-2 exposure only crystallises on an unexempted segment; F3's status is undetermined under RD-5.
RD-3(c) charges RydeTAXI waiting at the meter, not on the segment's exemption status; whether it follows the segment is unresolved while F3 is undetermined.
Accepted as far as it goes (F17 route disputes 0, F16) but the profile facts do not settle the RD-5 scope question that controls the outcome.
